recentItems.title: Review of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series
recentItems.description:
South Africa won the historic 2026 "Rugby's Greatest Rivalry" Test series 3-1 against New Zealand.

Springboks sealed the series victory on 12 September 2026 with a dominant 43-28 win over the All Blacks in the final Test match played at the M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, USA, in front of a North American record rugby crowd.

To talk to us about this series, we have roped in sport journalist and commentator Khanyiso Tshwaku.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Gauteng Education MEC Lebogang Maile briefs the media on the status of independent schools
recentItems.description:
Gauteng MEC for Education, Sport, Arts, Culture and Recreation, Lebogang Maile, will host a media briefing to provide a comprehensive update on the state of independent schools in Gauteng.

MEC Maile will provide an overview of the growth and performance of independent schools in the province, including government subsidies, registration and accountability requirements.

The briefing will also address the Department's interventions and action against illegally operating schools, as part of efforts to ensure that all learners have access to quality education in institutions that meet the required standards and regulatory requirements.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | ActionSA continues election campaign in Welkom
recentItems.description:
ActionSA Deputy President Dr Mbahare Kekana and Free State provincial leadership are on the ground in Welkom today. 

The party is embarking on a door-to-door campaign and will also visit the local taxi rank to woo voters ahead of the November local government elections. 

Our reporter Ishmael Modiba is following that campaign trail and has more.

recentItems.title: Heritage Month | Rhema Bible Church to host concert honouring Rev. Tiyo Soga's legacy
recentItems.description:
September is a month South Africans set aside to honour the people, practices and stories that have shaped who we are. And few stories are as overdue for the spotlight as that of Reverend Tiyo Soga.

For over 150 years, millions of South Africans have sung the hymn Lizalis' idinga lakho - without knowing the name of the man who wrote it. Reverend Soga was the first ordained Black South African minister of the Presbyterian Church, a writer, educator, translator, and advocate for the dignity of African people.

He will be honoured in a special commemorative concert on Saturday, 19 September 2026, at the Rhema Bible Church North in Randburg.

For more on this, we are joined by Author and Musician, Kutlwano Masote.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.
